# Screening Atlas

> Tenant screening rules and report coverage, state by state: application fee caps, what each screening report includes, and where criminal or eviction records may not appear. Every claim is linked to its source.

Screening Atlas is an independent reference site published by Atlas Guides. Every fee, rule and coverage claim links to the statute, government office or provider page it came from, and each page shows the date it was last checked. Where a figure could not be confirmed on a source page, the table shows a dash instead of a guess. Some outbound links are affiliate links; they are labeled and never change what a page says.

Last updated: 2026-11-28

## Guides

- [Fair Chance Housing Ordinances: Where Landlords Can't Screen for Criminal History](https://screeningatlas.com/fair-chance-housing-criminal-history-ordinances/): Seattle, Oakland and Portland limit or bar criminal-history screening of rental applicants. What each ordinance prohibits, which rentals are exempt, the Ninth Circuit ruling that changed Seattle's rule, Portland's 3- and 7-year look-backs, and the penalties. From the ordinances, the court opinion and each city's own pages. (checked 2026-11-28)
- [Lead-Based Paint Disclosure Before Signing a Lease: What Landlords Must Give Tenants](https://screeningatlas.com/lead-based-paint-disclosure-before-lease/): The federal lead disclosure rule for rentals built before 1978: which units it covers and which are exempt, the pamphlet, warning statement and signed disclosure a landlord must provide before the lease is signed, the 3-year recordkeeping rule, and penalties. From 40 CFR 745 subpart F, 24 CFR 35 subpart A and EPA's own pages. (checked 2026-11-28)
- [Move-In Condition Checklists and Photos: Which States Require Them](https://screeningatlas.com/move-in-condition-checklist-requirements-by-state/): Which states require a written move-in checklist, inspection report or photos before a landlord can take a security deposit or deduct for damage: Washington, Massachusetts, California, Arizona, Virginia, Michigan, Minnesota and Wisconsin. Deadlines, required wording and what happens without one, quoted from each statute. (checked 2026-11-28)
- [Security Deposit Return Deadlines by State, and When the Clock Starts](https://screeningatlas.com/security-deposit-return-deadlines-by-state/): How many days a landlord has to return a security deposit or send an itemized list in Florida, Arizona, Virginia, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio and Wisconsin, what starts the clock (move-out, end of the lease, a forwarding address), and what happens if the deadline is missed. Quoted from each statute. (checked 2026-11-28)
- [When Tenant Damage Is More Than the Security Deposit: Recovering the Rest, and Small Claims Limits by State](https://screeningatlas.com/tenant-damage-beyond-security-deposit-small-claims-limits/): The deposit is not a cap on what a tenant owes. What deposit statutes in Virginia, Florida, Arizona, Massachusetts and California say about claims beyond the deposit, and the small claims dollar limits in California, Massachusetts, Washington, Oregon, Virginia, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio, Arizona and Wisconsin, from each state's statute or court. (checked 2026-11-28)
- [Approving a Tenant With a Bigger Deposit or a Co-Signer: Is It Adverse Action?](https://screeningatlas.com/conditional-approval-higher-deposit-adverse-action/): If a credit or screening report is why you ask for a larger deposit, a co-signer, more rent or months up front, the FCRA treats it as adverse action and you owe a notice. Plus the deposit caps in California, Massachusetts and New York that limit what you can ask for. (checked 2026-11-27)
- [Can a Landlord Deduct Carpet Cleaning and Repainting From a Security Deposit?](https://screeningatlas.com/security-deposit-cleaning-repainting-wear-and-tear/): What California, Massachusetts, Washington, Oregon and New York law say about normal wear and tear, professional carpet cleaning, repainting after a long tenancy, itemized statements, deadlines and penalties. Quoted from each statute or the state's official guide. (checked 2026-11-27)
- [Does the Applicant's Employer Exist? Checking State Business Records](https://screeningatlas.com/verify-applicant-employer-business-records/): How to check that an applicant's employer is a real, registered business using official state business-entity searches (Delaware, California, Oregon, Washington, Texas), what those records show and don't, and what an employment verification service like The Work Number says it provides. (checked 2026-11-27)
- [How Far Back Does a Tenant Background Check Go?](https://screeningatlas.com/how-far-back-tenant-background-checks-go/): The FCRA seven-year limit on evictions, collections and arrests, the exception for criminal convictions (15 U.S.C. 1681c), and the stricter state limits in California, Washington and Oregon. (checked 2026-11-27)
- [Is the Previous Landlord Real? Checking Property Records Before a Reference Call](https://screeningatlas.com/verify-previous-landlord-property-records/): A fake job, fake pay stubs and a friend posing as the last landlord: how to check who owns the applicant's previous address using official county and city property records, with examples from New York City, Cook County, King County, Washington D.C. and Hennepin County. (checked 2026-11-27)
- [Can a Landlord Report Unpaid Rent to the Credit Bureaus? Furnisher Duties and How It Works](https://screeningatlas.com/reporting-unpaid-rent-to-credit-bureaus/): How landlords report unpaid rent or a move-out balance to Equifax, Experian and TransUnion, what the FCRA requires of anyone who furnishes that data (15 U.S.C. 1681s-2), how long it can stay on a report, California's notice rule, and what FrontLobby says it needs and charges. (checked 2026-11-25)
- [How Long Should a Landlord Keep Tenant Screening Reports, and How to Destroy Them](https://screeningatlas.com/how-long-to-keep-tenant-screening-reports/): What the FTC Disposal Rule (16 CFR part 682) requires when you get rid of tenant screening reports, how long SmartMove, RentRedi and Rentec Direct keep reports viewable, the FCRA lawsuit deadline, and state disposal laws in California, Massachusetts and Oregon. (checked 2026-11-25)
- [Illinois Rental Fee Rules for 2027: the $50 Application Fee Limit and Fee Disclosure](https://screeningatlas.com/illinois-rental-fee-rules-2027/): What Illinois Public Act 104-0479 (765 ILCS 705/35) changes for leases entered into after its January 1, 2027 effective date: the $50 limit on application and background check fees, the 14-day receipt rule, fees that must be on the first page of the lease, and the banned "junk fees", quoted from the statute. (checked 2026-11-25)
- [Is It Illegal to Run Credit or Background Checks in California? What State Law Actually Limits](https://screeningatlas.com/california-tenant-screening-rules/): California landlords can run credit and background checks, but state law limits the fee, requires written criteria and a copy of the credit report, bars certain criminal records and blanket bans, and requires an alternative to credit history for voucher holders. Quoted from Cal. Civ. Code 1950.6, Gov. Code 12955 and the state's 2026 landlord-tenant guide. (checked 2026-11-25)
- [Rental Listing Scams: "No Credit Check" Ads, $1 Credit-Check Links and Copied Listings](https://screeningatlas.com/rental-listing-scams-no-credit-check/): How rental listing scams work according to the FTC's December 2025 data spotlight ($65 million in reported losses since 2020), why a "landlord" asking for your credit score screenshot or a $1 credit check link is a red flag, how real tenant screening works, and what landlords whose listings get copied can do. (checked 2026-11-25)
- [Tenant Screening Reports Compared: What Each One Actually Includes](https://screeningatlas.com/tenant-screening-report-comparison/): SmartMove, TurboTenant, RentRedi, Rentec Direct, RentPrep and DoorLoop side by side: price, who pays, what is in each report, and the state-by-state gaps each provider discloses. Quoted from their own pages. (checked 2026-11-25)
- [Calling a Previous Landlord: References, Rental Verification and the FCRA](https://screeningatlas.com/previous-landlord-references-and-the-fcra/): When is a landlord reference just a phone call, and when does it become a consumer report under the FCRA? The federal definitions, the state rules that mention reference checks (CA, WA, OR, MN), and what TurboTenant and RentPrep say about verifying rental history. (checked 2026-11-24)
- [Charged a Screening Fee but Never Screened: Refund Rules by State](https://screeningatlas.com/screening-fee-refund-when-no-screening/): If a landlord collects an application or background-check fee and never runs the check, or fills the unit first, when must the money come back? The refund rules and penalties in California, Oregon, Minnesota, Maryland and Washington, quoted from each statute. (checked 2026-11-24)
- [How Long Does Tenant Screening Take? Turnaround and Report Access by Provider](https://screeningatlas.com/how-long-tenant-screening-takes/): How long a tenant background check takes on SmartMove, TurboTenant, RentRedi and Rentec Direct, what causes delays (identity verification, manual TransUnion checks, county criminal searches), and how long each lets you view the report, from their own help pages. (checked 2026-11-24)
- [How to Get a Free Copy of Your Tenant Screening Report Before You Apply](https://screeningatlas.com/free-tenant-screening-report-copy/): Renters can ask tenant screening companies for their own file. The federal free-report rules, the CFPB list of tenant screening companies with their contact pages, and what SmartMove, SafeRent, RealPage, CIC and Experian RentBureau say about requesting a copy. (checked 2026-11-24)
- [Section 8 and Source-of-Income Rules by State: Vouchers, Income Minimums and Credit Checks](https://screeningatlas.com/source-of-income-and-voucher-rules-by-state/): Can you refuse a housing voucher, and how does a "3x the rent" income rule apply to a voucher holder? What the statutes say in Washington, Oregon, California, Massachusetts and Minnesota, quoted and linked. (checked 2026-11-24)
- [Landlord Tenant Screening Kit: Criteria, Application and Adverse Action Templates](https://screeningatlas.com/kit/): A 16-page kit for small landlords: written screening criteria, rental application, consumer report authorization, FCRA adverse action notice templates, and a state cheat sheet on fee caps, criteria rules and criminal-history limits. PDF plus editable Word and Excel files. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [Medical Debt on a Rental Applicant's Credit Report: What Was Removed and Which States Ban It](https://screeningatlas.com/medical-debt-on-tenant-credit-reports/): Paid medical collections, collections under $500 and debts less than a year old no longer appear on Equifax, Experian and TransUnion reports. New York and Minnesota go further and bar consumer reporting agencies from reporting medical debt; California bars furnishing it. What that means for a tenant screening credit report. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [Rent Reporting to Credit Bureaus: TurboTenant, RentRedi, Avail and Innago Compared](https://screeningatlas.com/rent-reporting-services-compared/): Which landlord platforms report on-time rent to TransUnion, Experian and Equifax, what it costs, who pays, whether past months count, and California's rule requiring larger landlords to offer rent reporting. From each provider's own pages and Civil Code 1954.07. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [Screening a Guarantor or Co-Signer: Fees, Consent and How Each Platform Handles It](https://screeningatlas.com/screening-guarantors-and-co-signers/): Can you run a credit check on a guarantor and charge them an application fee? What California and Washington law say about guarantors, the FCRA consent basis, and how TurboTenant, RentRedi and SmartMove screen co-signers, from their own help pages. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [Screening an Applicant Without a Social Security Number: Which Services Accept an ITIN](https://screeningatlas.com/tenant-screening-without-ssn-itin/): SmartMove needs a valid SSN; TurboTenant and RentRedi accept an ITIN; Rentec Direct says its databases need an SSN. Provider-by-provider rules from their own help pages, plus Oregon's list of IDs a landlord must accept and California's ban on immigration-status questions. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [Tenant Screening Checker by State: Fee Rules, Coverage and Which Report Fits](https://screeningatlas.com/tenant-screening-checker-by-state/): Pick your state and get the application fee rule, whether a reusable report waives the fee, where TransUnion SmartMove can return criminal and eviction records, and which screening packages fit under the cap. Free, runs in your browser, every rule linked to its source. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [Written Tenant Screening Criteria: Where You Must Give Applicants Your Rules Before Charging a Fee](https://screeningatlas.com/written-tenant-screening-criteria-by-state/): Oregon, Washington, Minnesota and California each require landlords to put their screening criteria in writing and hand them to the applicant before (or when) taking a screening fee. What each statute requires, the deadline, and the penalty, quoted from the official code. (checked 2026-11-23)
- [Adverse Action Notices After a Tenant Screening Report: What Landlords Must Send](https://screeningatlas.com/adverse-action-notice-tenant-screening/): If you deny an applicant, or ask for a co-signer, a bigger deposit or higher rent, because of something in a screening report, federal law (FCRA section 615(a), 15 U.S.C. 1681m) requires a notice naming the screening company. What it must say, when a credit score must be disclosed, and the extra Washington and Oregon rules. Quoted from the statutes. (checked 2026-11-22)
- [Bank-Linked Income Verification: What the Landlord Actually Sees](https://screeningatlas.com/bank-linked-income-verification-what-landlords-see/): When an applicant connects a bank or payroll account during tenant screening, what lands on the landlord's screen? RentRedi (Plaid), TurboTenant (Snappt) and SmartMove income verification compared: report sections, price, who pays, and whether the applicant can skip it. From each provider's own help pages. (checked 2026-11-22)
- [Can a Landlord Take Rent Up Front? Prepaid Rent Limits in CA, MA, NY, HI and OR](https://screeningatlas.com/prepaid-rent-limits-by-state/): An applicant offers six months of rent in advance to make up for thin credit. Can you accept it? California allows it on a lease of six months or more; Massachusetts, New York and Hawaii cap what you can collect at move-in; Oregon treats a last month's rent deposit as a security deposit. Quoted from each statute or the state's official guide. (checked 2026-11-22)
- [Holding Deposits and "Admin Fees" vs Application Fees: Which States Regulate Each](https://screeningatlas.com/holding-deposits-and-admin-fees-by-state/): An applicant is charged a $75 application fee, a $150 admin fee and a $45 screening fee. Which of those are legal? Holding-deposit and move-in fee rules in Washington, Oregon, California, Massachusetts, Hawaii and New York, quoted from the statutes and the New York Attorney General's guide. (checked 2026-11-22)
- [Rent Collection App Fees Compared: ACH, Card and Payout Times](https://screeningatlas.com/rent-collection-app-fees/): What TurboTenant, RentRedi, Rentec Direct, Avail, Innago and DoorLoop charge per online rent payment (bank transfer and card), who pays the fee, and how long it takes the money to reach the landlord. Quoted from each provider's pricing and help pages. (checked 2026-11-22)
- [SmartMove Coverage by State: Where Criminal and Eviction Records Can Come Back](https://screeningatlas.com/smartmove-criminal-eviction-coverage-by-state/): All 50 states and D.C.: whether TransUnion SmartMove says its criminal report can return records there, and whether its eviction report is available, limited (with the affected counties) or not available. From SmartMove's own disclaimer and county list. (checked 2026-11-22)
- [Oregon Tenant Screening Rules: Fees, Criminal History, Evictions and Denial Letters](https://screeningatlas.com/oregon-tenant-screening-rules/): Oregon landlord screening rules from ORS 90.295, 90.303, 90.304 and 90.306: one screening charge per 60 days, the written notice required before you take it, which criminal records and evictions you may not consider, the 14-day denial statement, and the individualized assessment. Quoted from the statute. (checked 2026-11-21)
- [Phased (Two-Step) Tenant Screening: Cook County, D.C., New York City and New Jersey](https://screeningatlas.com/phased-tenant-screening-jurisdictions/): In some places a landlord must finish the non-criminal screening, and in some a conditional offer, before running a criminal background check. The rules for Cook County IL, Washington DC, New York City and New Jersey side by side: when the check is allowed, the look-back periods, the applicant's response window and who is exempt. Quoted from each law. (checked 2026-11-21)
- [Tenant Screening Cost Calculator: Landlord Pays vs. Applicant Pays](https://screeningatlas.com/tenant-screening-cost-calculator/): Work out what tenant screening costs you per vacancy and per year if you pay, versus what each applicant pays if they do, using the published prices for SmartMove, TurboTenant, RentRedi, Rentec Direct, RentPrep and DoorLoop. Prices checked against each provider page. (checked 2026-11-21)
- [Where to Look Up Eviction Records: Official Court Portals by State](https://screeningatlas.com/eviction-records-official-court-portals/): Free official court portals where landlords can check an applicant's eviction (landlord-tenant) cases in Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Massachusetts, Washington and Missouri, what each one leaves out, and the state rules that hide or limit eviction records in California, Minnesota, Washington, Wisconsin and Oregon. (checked 2026-11-21)
- [Alternatives to Zillow Rental Manager Screening: What Each Includes and Who Pays](https://screeningatlas.com/alternatives-to-zillow-rental-manager-screening/): Zillow Rental Manager screening is free for landlords and charges the applicant $40. Here is what it includes and how Apartments.com, Avail, SmartMove, TurboTenant, RentRedi, Rentec Direct, RentPrep and DoorLoop compare on who pays and what comes back. Quoted from their own pages. (checked 2026-11-20)
- [Reusable Tenant Screening Reports: Which States Make Landlords Accept Them](https://screeningatlas.com/reusable-tenant-screening-reports-by-state/): Colorado requires landlords to accept portable tenant screening reports; Washington and California let landlords choose but set rules; New York, Rhode Island and Wisconsin waive screening fees when the applicant brings a recent report. Quoted from each statute. (checked 2026-11-19)
- ["No Criminal Records Are Available" on a TurboTenant Report: What It Means](https://screeningatlas.com/turbotenant-no-criminal-records-available/): Why a TurboTenant screening report can show "No criminal records are available" even for an applicant with a record, what TurboTenant's own help center says about state suppression rules, and what landlords can do next. (checked 2026-11-18)
- [Rental Application Fee Caps by State (2026)](https://screeningatlas.com/application-fee-caps-by-state/): What landlords may charge rental applicants in 15 states, quoted from each state's statute: dollar caps, actual-cost rules, outright bans, and refund duties. Every row links to the law. (checked 2026-11-18)
